meta.note: machine-written (Claude), not reviewed by a native speaker
meta.about: Words the German course and the Carinthian village's content use that the word packs don't have, for a learner of German without a German dictionary (a download, LANI_LEXICON_URL) and for the printed sheets: the verbs and their present forms (sein, haben, heißen), the personal pronouns, the articles (der, die, das; ein, eine), the numbers, the greetings. Austrian standard first (Jänner, Paradeiser, Grüß Gott, Servus, Baba), the German-German word named in the gloss. Each has its meaning in Slovene and Italian (meanings), the English in gloss, flagged machine-written. Each part of the German course appends its units' words. Opa Sepp's newer stories (the Prince's Stone, the Kufenstechen, the Nikolo and the Krampus, and the rest) and the corner's newer readings add every word their German lines use, so a tap on one means it: the everyday words (mit, man, nur, war, ging), the verbs' past forms, the places and names (Dobratsch, Karawanken, Myra) and the Slovene words they quote (štehvanje, prvi rej). Since 2026-11-02 (supplement-coverage) also every other word of Kärnten's content a tap met nothing for: the ten older stories, the chest's readings, the scenes, the project steps, the arrivals, the sky and the villagers' lines (Hütte, schmecken, Kasermandl, Laurentiustränen), each with the forms the content uses, made from its paradigm; the packs' words again where the pack lacks a form the content uses (Händen, fängt), with the pack's meanings; the interjections with a meaning (hm, juhu, oje, psst); the grammar book's terms and endings; and the Slovene words the German lines quote, said to be Slovene in every base (hvala, dober dan, kozolec). Since 2026-11-02 (parties-kaernten) also every word the five ages' parties use (the Firstfeier, the Dorffest, the Wiesenmarkt, the Stadtfest), with the forms they use. Since 2026-11-03 (course-de-b2-c) also the words of German B2's units 13-18, and spoken Carinthian to understand (lei, nit, eppes, ofn, miad, letz, losn, Pfiati), said to be spoken in every base.
